title: Editorial: Coexistence Must Be More Than a Slogan
titleJp: 社説[しゃせつ]：「共生[きょうせい]」を掛[か]け声[ごえ]で終[お]わらせるな

sentences.jp: 少子[しょうし]高齢化[こうれいか]に伴[ともな]う人手[ひとで]不足[ぶそく]を背景[はいけい]に、外国人[がいこくじん]労働者[ろうどうしゃ]の受[う]け入[い]れ拡大[かくだい]が既定[きてい]路線[ろせん]となって久[ひさ]しい。
sentences.en: Against the backdrop of labor shortages brought on by a declining birthrate and an aging population, expanding the intake of foreign workers has long been the established course.

sentences.jp: 政府[せいふ]は「多文化[たぶんか]共生[きょうせい]」を掲[かか]げ、制度[せいど]の整備[せいび]を進[すす]めてきたが、その実態[じったい]が掛[か]け声[ごえ]に追[お]いついているとは言[い]い難[がた]い。
sentences.en: The government has held up the banner of "multicultural coexistence" and pressed ahead with building the necessary systems, but it is hard to say that the reality has caught up with the slogan.

sentences.jp: 技能[ぎのう]実習[じっしゅう]制度[せいど]をめぐっては、劣悪[れつあく]な労働[ろうどう]環境[かんきょう]や転職[てんしょく]の制限[せいげん]が長年[ながねん]批判[ひはん]されてきた。
sentences.en: The Technical Intern Training Program has long been criticized for poor working conditions and restrictions on changing jobs.

sentences.jp: 新[あら]たな「育成[いくせい]就労[しゅうろう]」制度[せいど]への移行[いこう]はその反省[はんせい]に立[た]ったものだが、看板[かんばん]を掛[か]け替[か]えるだけでは問題[もんだい]の根[ね]は断[た]てない。
sentences.en: The shift to the new Employment for Skill Development system is grounded in reflection on those failures, but merely changing the signboard will not cut out the root of the problem.

sentences.jp: 問[と]われているのは、受[う]け入[い]れた人々[ひとびと]を「労働力[ろうどうりょく]」としてではなく、地域[ちいき]で暮[く]らす「生活者[せいかつしゃ]」として遇[ぐう]する覚悟[かくご]があるかどうかである。
sentences.en: What is being tested is whether we are prepared to treat the people we accept not as "labor" but as "residents" who live in our communities.

sentences.jp: 日本語[にほんご]教育[きょういく]の機会[きかい]、子[こ]どもの就学[しゅうがく]支援[しえん]、医療[いりょう]や行政[ぎょうせい]サービスへのアクセス――いずれも、自治体[じちたい]やボランティアの善意[ぜんい]に依存[いぞん]している面[めん]が否[いな]めない。
sentences.en: Opportunities for Japanese-language education, support for children's schooling, access to medical and government services: it cannot be denied that all of these depend to some extent on the goodwill of local governments and volunteers.

sentences.jp: 財源[ざいげん]も人材[じんざい]も乏[とぼ]しい小[ちい]さな自治体[じちたい]ほど、その負担[ふたん]は重[おも]くのしかかる。
sentences.en: The smaller the municipality, and the scarcer its funds and staff, the more heavily that burden weighs on it.

sentences.jp: 国[くに]が受[う]け入[い]れの旗[はた]を振[ふ]る以上[いじょう]、その後[ご]の生活[せいかつ]を支[ささ]える仕組[しく]みづくりにも責任[せきにん]を負[お]うべきだ。
sentences.en: As long as the national government is the one waving the flag for accepting foreign workers, it should also bear responsibility for creating systems that support their lives afterward.

sentences.jp: 一方[いっぽう]で、受[う]け入[い]れる側[がわ]の社会[しゃかい]の意識[いしき]も問[と]われる。
sentences.en: At the same time, the attitudes of the receiving society are also being called into question.

sentences.jp: ごみ出[だ]しのルールや騒音[そうおん]をめぐる摩擦[まさつ]は、しばしば「文化[ぶんか]の違[ちが]い」の一言[ひとこと]で片付[かたづ]けられがちだ。
sentences.en: Friction over garbage rules and noise is often brushed aside with the single phrase "cultural differences."

sentences.jp: だが、その多[おお]くは必要[ひつよう]な情報[じょうほう]が届[とど]いていないことに起因[きいん]しており、丁寧[ていねい]な説明[せつめい]と対話[たいわ]によって解消[かいしょう]できるものも少[すく]なくない。
sentences.en: But much of it stems from necessary information not reaching people, and no small part of it can be resolved through careful explanation and dialogue.

sentences.jp: 隣人[りんじん]として顔[かお]の見[み]える関係[かんけい]を築[きず]くことこそ、偏見[へんけん]や排除[はいじょ]を防[ふせ]ぐ何[なに]よりの手立[てだ]てとなろう。
sentences.en: Building relationships as neighbors who know each other's faces is surely the best means of preventing prejudice and exclusion.

sentences.jp: 人口[じんこう]減少[げんしょう]が避[さ]けられない以上[いじょう]、外国人[がいこくじん]とともに地域[ちいき]を支[ささ]えていくことは、もはや選択肢[せんたくし]の一[ひと]つではなく前提[ぜんてい]である。
sentences.en: Since population decline is unavoidable, sustaining our communities together with foreign residents is no longer one option among many; it is a given.

sentences.jp: 「共生[きょうせい]」を掛[か]け声[ごえ]で終[お]わらせず、実[じつ]のあるものにできるかどうか。
sentences.en: Can we make "coexistence" into something real, rather than letting it end as a slogan?

sentences.jp: それは、この国[くに]の将来[しょうらい]の姿[すがた]そのものを左右[さゆう]する問[と]いにほかならない。
sentences.en: That is nothing less than a question that will determine the very shape of this country's future.

questions.q: What is the editorial's central argument?
choices: Japan should reduce the number of foreign workers it accepts
Foreign workers must be treated as residents of the community, not just as labor
Renaming the trainee program has solved its problems

questions.q: According to the editorial, much of the friction over garbage and noise is caused by what?
choices: A lack of laws on the issue

questions.q: Who does the editorial say should take responsibility for building support systems?
choices: The national government, since it is promoting the intake
